name: cobra-adbc8813-blind26-ots
instr:
# Repairing a Go CLI-building library without a test suite

We vendor this library and lean on it to give our own programs their terminal interface. After pulling a new copy of the tree, an alarming spread of unrelated behaviour changed at once. Nothing below is ordered by where we suspect the problem lives, because we have no idea; it is only what we can reproduce from the outside. The repository has received 26 separate undocumented edits.

Start with what happens when someone types an invocation. A program whose rule says it takes no free-standing words now runs happily when one stray word is passed, instead of refusing it as unexpected; the same hole shows up once a child action has been removed from a program's tree, since typing the removed child's name still succeeds rather than failing. A program whose rule allows at most N free-standing words refuses an invocation that supplies exactly N of them, claiming there are too many. While a typed line is being scanned to work out which words stand free, a single-letter on/off switch now swallows the word that follows it, so a name typed directly behind such a switch vanishes from the list, though the long spelling of the same switch behaves as it always did.

Declared relationships between named options have stopped working in both directions at once. Declaring a set mutually exclusive, or required together, or one-of-required, currently draws no complaint at all: passing two members of an exclusive pair, or only one member
